hint.redirect: {name} opens your company’s own sign-in page.

message.cancelled: The sign-in was cancelled. Nothing happened — you can try again.
message.notMember: This account is not a member of this workspace. Ask its administrator to invite you, then sign in again.
message.providerError: The identity provider could not complete the sign-in. Try again; if it keeps failing, it is on their side rather than yours.
message.incomplete: The sign-in came back incomplete. Start it again from here.
message.expired: That sign-in took too long and has expired. Start a fresh one.
message.unmatched: That sign-in could not be matched to the one that started. Start a fresh one.
message.failed: The sign-in could not be completed. Try again.
message.unknown: The sign-in did not complete. Try again.
message.cardFailed: That did not complete. Check the card is in the reader and try again.
message.signedOut: You are signed out of {app}. If you used your company’s own sign-in, it stays signed in on this computer: on a shared computer, sign out of it too.
message.ended: Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again.
message.noWays: No way to sign in is set up here. Tell whoever runs this deployment.

missing.title: The card software is not running
missing.lead: Signing in with a card needs the ID-software and its browser extension on this computer. Install it, then try again — nothing here has to be redone.

signIn.title: Sign in to the admin app
signIn.lead: This is the admin app, where the workspace is set up. Everyday work stays in {product} at its usual address.

nothing.title: Nothing here for you to configure
nothing.lead: You are signed in, but no part of this workspace's configuration is yours. An administrator can give you access. Your everyday work is in {product}.

down.title: The admin app is not answering
down.lead: Nothing was changed. Try again in a minute. If it keeps happening, tell whoever runs this deployment.

page.lead: The configuration of this workspace, carried out as one file and back in.

network.title: The admin app is not open from here
network.lead: This address answers only inside the networks your organisation set for it. Your everyday work is in {product} at its usual address.

assurance.title: This sign-in is not strong enough here
assurance.lead: The admin app asks for a stronger sign-in than the one you used. Sign in with an ID card, or with a sign-in your organisation counts as strong.

frame.logoutFailed: Signing out did not complete. Try again.
frame.languageFailed: Changing the language did not complete. Try again.

export.title: Export
export.lead: Your whole configuration as one file — to keep, to hand to another workspace, or to edit and bring back.
export.failed: The configuration could not be downloaded: {reason}

import.title: Import
import.lead: Drop a configuration file. Nothing is written until you have seen exactly what it would do — and then either all of it lands, or none of it.
import.drop: Drop a file here, or click to choose one

rejected.type: That is not a configuration file — choose the .json file an export downloaded.
rejected.count: Drop one file at a time.

carries.register: The list of services and their boxes this deployment runs on
carries.notToday: Not in it today: roles, user types, the chart of authority.

change.name: its name changes
change.labels: its names in other languages change
change.status: whether it is in use changes

refusal.keyConflict: It already means something else here, and what an item is never changes. Add a new one with the meaning you want, and take this one out of use.
refusal.unknownReference: It names something this workspace does not have, or has taken out of use. Name one that is in use, or add it in the file too.
refusal.inUse: It is still in use here, so the file cannot take it away. Move what uses it first, then drop the file again.
refusal.numberTaken: Its number already belongs to something else here. Give it a number of its own in the file.

skip.deploymentOwned: This deployment's list says otherwise; only whoever runs the deployment changes it.

reason.noBox: you do not hold the box that imports it

workspace.bothUnnamed: This file names a workspace and a corporate login.

workspace.keptUnnamed: Neither is taken from a file: this workspace keeps its own name and its own corporate login.

badge.lands: clean — lands only with the rest

note.failed: {area} did not answer, so its part of the file could not be judged.
note.skipped: No service in this workspace owns this part, so it is not applied here — the rest of the file can be.

stop.refused: {n} item was refused, so this file cannot be applied — none of it. Change it in the file (the reason says what) and drop the file again. | {n} items were refused, so this file cannot be applied — none of it. Change them in the file (each reason says what) and drop the file again.
stop.refusedArea: {areas} refused this file, so none of it can be applied. Change what the reason says, then drop the file again.
stop.failed: {areas} did not answer, so this file could not be judged. Nothing was written. Preview again in a moment.
stop.bad: This file cannot be read as a configuration document. Nothing was written. Drop a file exported from this screen.
stop.other: The file could not be previewed: {reason}

act.downloadNow: Download the configuration as it is now

applied.head: Applied.
applied.rest: The whole file is in force.

moved.head: The configuration changed after your preview.
moved.rest: Nothing was written. Preview again to see what this file would do now — the new preview shows anyone else's change it would overwrite.

refused.head: Refused at Apply.
refused.rest: Something the configuration itself does not cover changed after your preview. Nothing was written — the refused item below says what.

failed.head: Nothing was written.
failed.rest: A service could not write its part, so the rest of the file was withheld.

rolledBack.head: Rolled back, except what it added.
rolledBack.headNone: Nothing of this file is in force.
rolledBack.rest: {failed} could not write its part after {written} had written its own, so it was restored to what it held before. | {failed} could not write its part after {written} had written theirs, so they were restored to what they held before.
rolledBack.kept: A restore never removes, so what the file added is still here:
rolledBack.outOfUse: In use nowhere yet. Take it out of use in {areas} if you do not want it. | In use nowhere yet. Take them out of use in {areas} if you do not want them.

partial.head: Only part of this file is in force.
partial.rest: A service could not write its part, and restoring the part written before it failed too. Preview again: the new preview shows exactly what is still to land, and applying it completes the file.

other.head: The file could not be applied.

line.applied: {n} change landed, recorded in History under your name | {n} changes landed, recorded in History under your name
line.appliedNothing: nothing in it changes this part
line.withheld: clean, not applied because another part did not land
line.refused: nothing of this part was written
line.notWritten: its service did not answer. Nothing of this part was written.
line.refusedPart: it refused its part: {reason}. Nothing of this part was written.
line.rolledBack: restored to what it held before this import
line.rolledBackKept: restored: every change is back as it was, except what the file added
line.notRestored: holds this file's part — the restore after the failure did not succeed
line.skipped: not applied here — no service in this workspace owns it
